about: Guards one of your holdings (since 0.16 the guard loop the ruler's lieutenant wrote in test A1, made the standard): the lord rides a loop of the holding and its villages (places; left out, the holding and then its villages, nearest first), stays stay_hours at each stop, and takes the volunteers there. Lords named in lords ride the same loop with him as one group (give each the same places and start_stop, and each a different turn): at each stop they wait for one another (8 hours at most), one of them takes the volunteers while the others stand by, and the turn passes on at the next stop, so each gets his share; when no lord of the group has a volunteer within his reach left at a stop, they ride on after an hour. He weighs every fight by the game's own marching and battle rules: an enemy lord or army, or a band of bandits, within reach_hours of his own march and near his loop, he strikes only when the enemies who could be there by the middle of the fight and by its end (the hours to reach it and the fight's own length, worked out each time from both sides' strength) are at most strike_below of your side there; he keeps weighing as he chases, and breaks off a chase that would lead out of his area or has not closed in for 6 hours. Of the guards of a holding only as many go at an enemy as it takes: the nearest first (then the strongest), until together they are enough times the strength it fights with; the others keep to the loop. Your ruler's own attack within reach he joins the same way, as far as three times his reach from the holding. A siege of the holding he breaks when the besiegers, with everyone who could come to their aid in time, are at most strike_below of your side with the defenders inside who would sally out. He shelters from forces that could reach him before he got behind walls once they are shelter_at times your side by him, in the nearest castle or town he reaches first whose defenders, with him, would hold it, and comes out once they have passed. He buys his own food when he runs low; turn 0 also carries food to the holding when its stores fall below half of days of siege (with his march there). When an enemy army, or the strongest enemy lord near, is seen marching on the holding, every guard rides in with his spare food to fill its stores and stays inside for the siege, but only if its defenders, with them, would hold it against that force; if they would not, he shelters elsewhere rather than be shut in and taken with it (stay_inside 1: he rides in all the same). It ends when the holding falls.
calls_back: the holding falls, is besieged by a force too strong to break, or an enemy marches on it (he rides in to stand the siege, or shelters elsewhere when it would not hold); he strikes, breaks off or gives up a chase, joins your ruler's attack, shelters from or comes out after a strong force, or carries food to the holding

takes.at: own_holding: the holding guarded and fed
takes.places: friendly_holding: the loop, in order: the holding and its villages
takes.lords: the other lords of his group, who ride the loop with him and take turns at the volunteers (up to 4)

reach_hours: how many hours of his own march out he looks for enemies to strike, and for danger
stay_hours: hours at each stop of the loop
start_stop: which stop of the loop he starts at (from 0); the same for every lord of a group
turn: his place in the group's turns at the volunteers (from 0), a different one for each lord of a group; turn 0 also carries food to the holding
strike_below: strike only when the enemies who can be there by the middle and by the end of the fight are at most this share of your side there
shelter_at: shelter when the forces that could reach him before he could get behind walls are this many times your side's strength by him
days: keep the holding's food at this many days of siege: turn 0 rides to feed it when it has fewer than half of this, plus his march there
enough: guards go at an enemy, the nearest first (then the strongest), until together they are this many times the strength it fights with; the rest keep to the loop (not for breaking a siege, which takes all)
stay_inside: 1: when an enemy marches on the holding, ride in and stand the siege even if its defenders, with the guards, would not hold it (if it falls, he is taken with it); 0: only when they would hold
